definition: In computer science, an instance or token (from metalogic and metamathematics) is a specific occurrence of a software element that is based on a type definition.
details: When created, an occurrence is said to have been instantiated, and both the creation process and the result of creation are called instantiation.
story: Imagine a chef tasting every ingredient before it goes into the pot, deciding what belongs and what would ruin the broth. Think of it this way: In computer science, an instance or token (from metalogic and metamathematics) is a specific occurrence of a software element that is based on a type definition. And here is the clever part: When created, an occurrence is said to have been instantiated, and both the creation process and the result of creation are called instantiation. It is the raw material; the model is only ever as good as what it was fed. And that is Instance (computer science) — the unglamorous work everything else stands on.
